sourceClaimsReview.treatment: Countrywide generalisation explicitly unverified; excluded from factual analysis.

editorialReview.intent: Preserve the source argument about selective outrage; add a concrete equal-standards and document-evidence method without endorsing theft or declaring unverified corruption.
editorialReview.legalScope: Civic commentary using narrow primary provisions; no assessment of a particular contract’s validity or anyone’s criminal guilt.
editorialReview.keywordMetrics: No search-volume or ranking metrics claimed.
editorialReview.faqOmitted: A focused opinion-and-evidence essay does not need a manufactured FAQ.
editorialReview.numbersNotInvented: No demand for numeric charts is allowed to fabricate source quantities, ages, losses or ownership.

limitations: This is a third-party television excerpt shared by Eduard, not Eduard speaking or eyewitness testimony by him. The speaker and original broadcast date are not independently identified here.
Allegations about named politicians, a media owner and kiosk allocation are not independently established. Article avoids reproducing names as targets or asserting wrongdoing.
The number and ages of people, quantity/value of goods, ownership of individual kiosks, beneficial ownership, legal form of allocations and any corruption finding remain unverified.
The categorical comparison about kiosks in Greece and Italy is not verified or used as a factual premise.
Edited street/protest b-roll does not establish common provenance, timing or a single continuous event.
No loss total, ratio, public-loss estimate or comparative damage statistic can be responsibly calculated from this source.
